description: HydroCloud is a reusable web client for viewing hydrological observations from several providers. Martin Roberge and collaborators developed its JavaScript interface for mapping stream gauges, plotting discharge hydrographs and flow-duration curves, and inspecting watershed attributes. The README also documents widgets for webpages and Jupyter notebooks and local storage of selected data. Geographic coverage and record periods depend on the connected gauge services; the journal describes USGS and German WSV sources, not a uniform global monitoring series. The public client code is free under MIT. It can support selecting and checking observations before hydrological calibration and infrastructure water-risk studies, alongside the original provider services. A limitation is dependence on external endpoints and mapping layers: this review did not test current data retrieval or the hosted application. The repository contains client software, not ownership of the observations. No gauge time series were downloaded and no browser widget was executed.
name: HydroCloud hydrology data web client
notes: G5 G5-0211. Software checked through metadata and documentation, without installation or execution. Geographic scope follows the documented application or software portability; it does not imply validation throughout that area.
provider: Martin Roberge and HydroCloud contributors, Towson University
